heard: Galileo thought Saturn was three planets stuck together. He looked through his telescope and saw two massive ears. Scientists spent decades arguing over these weird, clinging side moons. Then, those mysterious moons simply vanished from the sky. Astronomers feared their own telescopes were failing them. Dutch astronomer Christian Huygens finally cracked the code in 1659. He realized the ears weren't moons or solid arms at all. Saturn was actually wearing a giant, flat, floating ring. This was the first time anyone discovered a ringed planet. It looked nothing like the three planets stuck together.
